los.text: Plot baby and child measurements on a growth chart and interpret the results.
los.html:
1
  • Use the correct chart (UK-WHO 0–4 years; UK 2–18 years; Down syndrome and preterm charts as needed)
  • Correct age (correct for prematurity until 2 years if born <37 weeks).
2Measure accurately: weight (naked infant), length (lying, <2 years) or height (standing), head circumference (largest around the occiput).
3Plot a dot at the right age and value; interpret the trend across centile lines.
PatternMeaning
Following a centileNormal (even on a low centile)
Crossing ≥2 major centile lines downwardsFaltering growth
Weight falling before length/heightUndernutrition
Height falling with weight preservedEndocrine cause (hypothyroidism, GH deficiency, steroids)
Head circumference crossing upwardsHydrocephalus

los.text: Recognise the key information required to identify failure to thrive in infants and children.
los.html:
Faltering growth (failure to thrive)
Weight falls across 1 centile (birth <9th centile), 2 centiles (9th–91st) or 3 centiles (>91st) (NICE NG75)
Weight below the 2nd centile
Newborn: weight loss >10% of birth weight; not back to birth weight by 3 weeks
Information neededFeeding history (amount, frequency, technique), vomiting/diarrhoea, birth history, development, illnesses, family heights, social circumstances, safeguarding (neglect)
CausesInadequate intake (most common), malabsorption (coeliac, CF), increased needs (heart disease), vomiting (reflux), neglect

los.text: Identify the most common causes of serious illness in children.
los.html:
Serious illness in children
Sepsis (including meningococcal)
Meningitis/encephalitis
Pneumonia, bronchiolitis, severe asthma
Dehydration (gastroenteritis), DKA
Kawasaki disease
Intussusception, appendicitis, volvulus
Non-accidental injury

los.text: Recognise the main warning signs of serious illness in children and respond appropriately.
los.html:
NICE traffic light: red features (high risk)
Colour: pale, mottled, ashen, blue
Activity: no response to social cues, appears ill, doesn't wake or stay awake, weak/high-pitched or continuous cry
Breathing: grunting, RR >60, moderate/severe chest indrawing
Circulation: reduced skin turgor
Other: age <3 months with temperature ≥38 °C, non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, neck stiffness, status epilepticus, focal signs, bile-stained vomiting
  • Respond: urgent paediatric assessment (999 in the community), ABCDE, sepsis pathway; safety-net amber cases.

los.text: Perform an initial clinical assessment of an unwell child, including history and physical examination.
los.html:
Assessment
History: from parent and child; onset, fever, feeding and fluid intake, wet nappies, vomiting/diarrhoea, breathing, rash, behaviour, immunisations, contacts, PMH
Observations: age-specific HR, RR, temperature, sats, CRT, (BP), PEWS
ABCDE examination with the child on the parent's lap; distraction; look before you touch
Hydration: mucous membranes, fontanelle, tears, CRT, skin turgor
Ears and throat last

los.text: Take a detailed and focused history from a patient with a hidden agenda, recognising potential challenges.
los.html:
Hidden agenda
Clues: vague or minor complaint, lingering at the end ("while I'm here…"), anxiety out of proportion, non-verbal cues
Elicit: open questions, ICE, "Is there anything else you'd like to talk about today?", explore cues, silence
Common hidden agendas: cancer fears, mental health, sexual health, domestic abuse, substance misuse, sick note
Challenges: embarrassment, fear, time pressure; respond without judgement

los.text: Understand the patient’s perspective and incorporate it into clinical decision-making.
los.html:
• Patient perspective (ICE, values, circumstances) shapes the plan: e.g. a lorry driver's livelihood with seizures
    • fear of a parent's illness
    • preferences about treatment.
    • Shared decision making: present options with risks/benefits and agree a plan that fits the patient.

los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the neck and thyroid with increased confidence and competence.
los.html:
• Neck and thyroid examination: see ICM Year 1 › Endocrine & diabetes › LO 4
    • aim for fluent sequence, palpation from behind with swallowing, eye signs, thyroid status, and clear presentation.
